sentence: This project tests whether small molecule inhibitors combined with T cell therapy can improve treatment of infants with a high-risk leukemia.
This project studies the structure and function of the human machinery that copies and reads mitochondrial DNA, to learn how mutations form.
This project studies why patients with metastatic gastrointestinal cancer differ in their use of targeted therapies and immunotherapies, using computer methods to read registry text.
This project builds analytical tools that examine differences within tumors using sequencing data from public databases.
This project tests whether a smartphone app with location tracking can help prevent relapse in patients treated for opioid use disorder.
This project uses artificial intelligence tools to work out causes of death from narratives collected from surviving caretakers.
This project studies how a complex silences the gamma-globin gene, to help develop treatment for sickle cell anemia.
This project uses genetically informed designs to study how parents' drinking and psychopathology relate to when adolescents start using alcohol.
This project uses optogenetics and a microfluidic cell-like approach to find how proteins help form macromolecular complexes at the plasma membrane.
This project offers sequencing, computer analysis and CRISPR genome engineering of B cells to study how plasma cells develop and are maintained.
This project builds a chip model of colorectal cancer from patient biopsy material to find what in the tumor microenvironment changes treatment response.
This project studies how phase separation builds biomolecular condensates that organize human cells, and what goes wrong in disease.
This project studies neural stem cells in zebrafish and planarians to learn how they regrow after spinal cord injury.
This project studies how bacteriophage T4 packages, stores and releases its viral genome, then builds a gene therapy vehicle for muscular dystrophy.
This project improves deep learning tools that detect senescent cells in nuclear-stained tissue sections and count them.
This project expands research resources and data science resources to study minority health and health disparities.
This project uses a mouse model to study how mutated cells grow in different tissues and how aging changes this process.
This project collects and processes plasma, urine and other samples from healthy people followed over time, using standardized methods, to catalogue the human virome.
This project builds an imaging system to study molecular and structural signs of mucosal healing in ulcerative colitis and predict relapse.
This project uses spatial imaging and single-cell RNA sequencing to study how lymph nodes are conditioned to allow metastasis of tumor cells.
